$comment: Canonical account-rule invariants, shared by the Python and TypeScript implementations.
Signup exists in two languages: services/users.py for the Streamlit app, and
web/lib/auth/contract.ts for the site. Importing one into the other is not
possible without standing up an HTTP service purely to avoid duplication,
which would add a failure mode to every signup to save a small amount of code.
So the two implementations are independent by design — and this file is what
stops them being two unrelated definitions. Both test suites read these exact
vectors, so a rule that changes on one side without the other fails on both.
Adding a rule means adding a vector here first.

email_normalization.$comment: Trim, then lowercase. Storage and lookup must agree, or the same address registers twice.
email_normalization.$comment_plus: The +tag is deliberately PRESERVED. Stripping it would silently merge addresses their owner treats as distinct, and is not something a mail provider guarantees.

email_validity.$comment: Deliberately permissive: the only authority on whether an address works is whether mail arrives. This rejects the obviously-not-an-address cases and nothing more.

opaque_username.$comment: Internal identifier for accounts whose owner never chose one. Must satisfy the pre-existing username constraint that every legacy username already satisfies.

derivation_probe.$comment: Generating from this account must not produce a username containing any of these fragments.

password_policy.$comment: Identical to what the 21.dev strength meter shows. The meter is UX; this is enforced server-side, and the two must not diverge or the form lies about what will be accepted.

new_account_defaults.$comment: State a site-created account must start in. Getting email_verification_required wrong here would silently grant new accounts the legacy exemption.

legacy_account_behaviour.$comment: Accounts predating the site flow. Backfilled by Alembic revision s9t0u1v2w3x4.
legacy_account_behaviour.$comment_exemption: Exempt, NOT falsely marked verified. email_verified_at stays null because nobody ever confirmed those addresses.

login_identifier_resolution.$comment: An identifier containing @ resolves by email ONLY, with no fallthrough to username. The rule is total because usernames cannot contain @.

bcrypt.$comment: Verified interoperable in both directions on 2026-08-11: a Node-generated hash validates in Python and vice versa.

$comment: The canonical four-field lifecycle for a site-created account.
Added 2026-08-12 after a report claimed email_verification_required stayed
true after verification. The implementation was correct and the report was
wrong, but nothing pinned the whole transition in one place, so the claim
could not be checked against a single source. Now it can.
The two flags mean different things and must not be conflated:
email_verification_required  does this account need verification at all
email_verified_at            has that verification actually happened
An account is blocked only when required AND not yet done.
account_state_transition.$comment_strategy: strategy_profile_completed stays false through every website step. The website never writes it; Streamlit's first-run Strategy Profile gate is what that false value drives.
account_state_transition.$comment_gate: verified_at non-null with required=true reads as VERIFIED, not blocked: the timestamp means the work was done. Unreachable through the real flow, since consuming a verification sets required=false.

$comment: Website -> Streamlit handoff. Issued in TypeScript (web/lib/auth/handoff.ts),
redeemed in Python (services/auth_handoff.py). The two are independent
implementations of one credential, so these invariants are what keeps them
compatible.
Token VALUES are random and must never match across languages. What is
pinned here is the shape: TTL, hash representation, entropy, and the fact
that the credential carries nothing.
handoff.$comment_claims: Empty, and deliberately so: no user id, username, email, expiry, session id, or account flag. The token is a lookup key, worthless without its row.

credential_separation.$comment: All three must remain distinct. The website cookie value must never appear in a URL, a JSON body, or any request bound for APP_ORIGIN, and must never be reused as the handoff or the Streamlit session.

eligibility.$comment: strategy_profile_completed must NOT be required. A new user is expected to arrive with it false; that false is what routes them to the first-run Strategy Profile. Requiring it would make the screen that sets it unreachable.
